verses.1: And David gathered all the chosen men of Israel, three hundred thousand in number.
verses.2: And David and all the people who were with him, from the leaders of Judah, went up to carry away the Ark of God from there. The name of God, the Almighty, is that which sits upon His throne.
verses.3: And they drove the Ark of God to a new altar. They carried it out of the house of Abinadab, which was in Gibeah. Uzzah and his brothers, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new altar.
verses.4: And he was taken away from the house of Abinadab, which was located in the field next to the altar of God. His brothers went ahead of him.
verses.5: And David, and all the houses of Israel, shall sing praises to the LORD in all the trees of the forest, in all kinds of shrubs, in all kinds of plants, and in all kinds of flowers.
verses.6: And they came to Goren Nakhon. They sent Uzza to the temple of God. But Uzza held onto him, because they had stolen it earlier that day.
verses.7: And Jehovah struck Ezah with his sword. There, the God struck down the people of Ezah. They died there, along with the entire army of the God.
verses.8: And David was angry because Jehovah had sent forth His wrath upon Uzzah. He called that place “Uzzah” until today.
verses.9: And David saw God on that day. He said, “How can the temple of God come to me?”
verses.10: And David did not want to remove the glory of Jehovah from the city of David. Therefore, David took it into the house of Adonai, the God of Israel.
verses.11: And Jehovah settled in the house of Adam, the servant. It was a three-story building. Jehovah blessed Adam’s servant and all who lived in his house.
verses.12: And David reported to King David, saying, “May the LORD bless the house of Adam and all those who belong to him through the service of the Lord. Then David went up with the Ark of God from the house of Adam to the city of David, in joy.
verses.13: And it happened that the priests carrying the Ark of God walked six steps forward, and they offered sacrifices and prayers.
verses.14: And David tried his best to please the LORD. David was very diligent in his efforts to please God.
verses.15: And David and all the houses of Israel shall lift up the ark of God in triumph and with loud voices.
verses.16: And the shadow of Jehovah fell upon the city of David. From the tent of Bath-Shalom, people looked out and saw King David being humiliated and trampled in front of Jehovah. They were filled with sorrow.
verses.17: And they brought the Ark of God, and displayed it in its place within the temple that David had built. David stood before God and Solomon also stood there.
verses.18: And David was able to bring up the offerings and sacrifices. He blessed the people in the name of Jehovah, the Army God.
verses.19: And he divided it among all the people of Israel, for every man and woman. Each person received one piece of bread, one portion of food. Then all the people went back to their homes.
verses.20: And David sat down to bless his house. Then the daughter of Saul went out from her room to meet David. She said, “What a great day it is today! King Israel has been revealed to his servants today. It’s as if one of the gods has been revealed.”
verses.21: And David said to Michal, “Before the LORD, who has chosen me from among my father’s household and from all his house, I will speak about Israel before the LORD. I will do what is right in the eyes of the LORD.”
verses.22: And I was still in a state of shame and humiliation. I was humiliated in the eyes of others, along with those who said that I would be destroyed.
verses.23: And Micah, the daughter of Shaul, would not have any children until the day of her death.
